questions.question: What is the use of Net National Product (NNP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To calculate per capita income **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is an important economic indicator that reflects the total value of all goods and services

 
 
• produced by a country’s citizens and businesses, both domestically and abroad
 
 
 
• The use of Net National Product is to calculate per capita income.
 
• Net National Product (NNP):
 
 
• NNP is obtained by subtracting depreciation value (i.e. capital stock consumption) from GNP.
 
 
 
• NNP reflects the true net income of an economy, it helps governments and businesses in planning for the long term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP):

 
 
• It is the total money value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of the country during a given period of time.
 
• GDP = C + G + I
 
 
• C = Consumption expenditure
 
• G = Government expenditure
 
• I = Investment expenditure
 
 
 
 
 
• Gross National Product (GNP):
 
 
• It refers to the money value of the total output of production of final goods and services produced by the nationals of a country during a given period of time, generally a year.
 
 
 
• National Income (NI):
 
 
• When NNP is calculated at factor cost (FC) it is called National Income.
 
• The measure is calculated by deducting indirect taxes and adding subsidies in NNP at Market Price (MP).
 
• In India, the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is the weighted average price of 676 items with the base year 2017-18.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury Planet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mercury** is the smallest planet in our solar system and is closest to the Sun.
 
• Its **orbital period around the Sun** is about 88 Earth days, making it the fastest planet.
 
• Because of its proximity to the Sun, Mercury experiences extreme temperature variations.
 
• It has **no natural satellites** or moons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturn**

 
 
• Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and is known for its prominent ring system.
 
• It has a total of 146 moons, with Titan being the largest.
 
• Saturn is a gas giant composed primarily of hydrogen and helium.
 
 
 
• **Uranus**
 
 
• Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and has a unique blue-green color due to methane in its atmosphere.
 
• It has a tilted axis, causing extreme seasonal variations.
 
• Uranus has 27 known moons, with Titania being the largest.
 
 
 
• **Jupiter**
 
 
• Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system and the fifth from the Sun.
 
• It has a strong magnetic field and at least 79 moons, with Ganymede being the largest.
 
• Jupiter is known for its Great Red Spot, a giant storm that has been raging for centuries.

questions.question: The parliamentary standing committees have a tenure of ________ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Parliamentary Standing Committees** in India have a tenure of **one year**
 
• **Parliamentary Standing Committees** in India are permanent committees that work throughout the year
 
 
• to scrutinize and oversee various aspects of legislation, government policies, and administration.
 
 
 
• They play a crucial role in enhancing the efficiency of parliamentary work by focusing on specific areas in detail. 
 
• These committees are divided based on different ministries and departments, such as Finance, Defense, Health, etc.
 
• There are currently **24 DRSCs**, with members drawn from both the Lok Sabha (lower house) and the Rajya Sabha (upper house).

questions.question: Which military officer led the British forces in the Battle of Chinhat fought in 1857?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Lawrence**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** British forces in the Battle of Chinhat ** **were led by Brigadier General Henry Lawrence.**
 
• However, the actual British force on the battlefield was commanded by **Colonel William Goldby**,
 
 
• who led a contingent of British troops and loyal sepoys.
 
 
 
• The **battle resulted in a decisive defeat for the British,** and following this, the British forces retreated to the Residency in Lucknow,
 
 
• where they faced a prolonged siege (**known as the Siege of Lucknow**)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Battle of Chinhat**

 
 
• The **Battle of Chinhat**, fought on **June 30, 1857**, was a significant early engagement during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• It took place near the town of Chinhat, on the outskirts of **Lucknow**. 
 
• The rebellion against British rule had spread across northern India, and **Lucknow**, the capital of the province of **Oudh (Awadh)**, became a key center of resistance
 
• The **Battle of Chinhat** was a decisive victory for the Indian rebels, and it marked the beginning of the **Siege of Lucknow**.

questions.question: The Supreme Court, in May 2023, observed that it can give divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage by exercising its discretionary power under ________.

options.text: Article 142 of the Constitution of India
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
Article 143 of the Constitution of India
Article 32 of the Constitution of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 142 of the Constitution of India**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India used Article 142(1) of the Indian Constitution to grant couples the right to divorce based on 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'.
 
• Article 142(1) of the Indian Constitution reads, "The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it...".
 
• The Supreme Court's decision expanded the grounds on which divorce can be sought in India.
 
• Previously, the grounds for divorce were outlined in individual personal laws and did not include the concept of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage' as it was not explicitly listed as grounds for divorce in any specific legislation. The 2023 ruling made it a valid reason to seek a divorce.
 
• The court used its discretionary powers to take cognizance of the realities of irreparable marriages and rule in favor of allowing legal terminations in such cases. This action sets a significant precedent for future cases involving such marital situations.
 
• This step by the Supreme Court could potentially pave the way for broader legal reform, rooting the law more firmly in the changing social context and conditions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 136 – Special Leave to Appeal to the Supreme Court****​**

 
 
• It Grants the Supreme Court discretionary power to allow special leave to appeal against any judgment, decree, or order in any cause or matter, passed by any court or tribunal.
 
• This article applies to both civil and criminal cases, giving broad powers to the Supreme Court to ensure justice.
 
• It cannot be used for appeals from judgments of military courts or tribunals.
 
 
 
• **Article 143 – Power of the President to Consult the Supreme Court**
 
 
• It Empowers the President of India to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance.
 
• The Supreme Court's advice is not binding on the President; it is a consultative process.
 
• **It is ** Used to clarify constitutional or legal issues, like the Ayodhya case and the Berubari case.
 
 
 
• **Article 32** – **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• **​It is one of the Fundamental Rights.**
 
• **It is the Heart and Soul of the Constitution.**
 
• It Empowers individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a medium - sized globular protein that acts as a pancreatic serine protease found in the digestive system of many vertebrates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trypsin**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The medium-sized globular protein you're referring to is **trypsin**
 
• **Trypsin is a pancreatic serine protease**, meaning it belongs to the class of enzymes that cleave peptide bonds in proteins. 
 
• It is f**ound in the digestive systems** of many vertebrates and plays a crucial role in protein digestion by breaking down proteins into smaller peptides
 
• It is **produced in the pancreas** as an inactive precursor, trypsinogen, which is activated in the small intestine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Amylase**

 
 
• It Breaks down starch into sugars (maltose and dextrin) during digestion.
 
• **It is ** Found in saliva (salivary amylase) and pancreas (pancreatic amylase).
 
• **It **Begins working in the mouth and continues in the small intestine.
 
• **It is** Vital for carbohydrate digestion and energy production.
 
 
 
• **Lipase**
 
 
• It Breaks down fats (lipids) into fatty acids and glycerol.
 
• It is produced in Pancreas (pancreatic lipase) and also in smaller amounts in the stomach.
 
• It Primarily acts in the small intestine.
 
• It is Essential for fat digestion and absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin**
 
 
• **It **Breaks down proteins into smaller peptides (proteolysis).
 
• **It is produced in **Stomach cells as an inactive precursor, pepsinogen, which is activated by stomach acid.
 
• **It** Works in the acidic environment of the stomach.
 
• **It is **Critical for initiating protein digestion in the stomach.

questions.question: Citizens are NOT discriminated against on the basis of religion, caste or sex because of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Equality.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Citizens are not discriminated against on the basis of religion, caste, or sex primarily because of the **Right to Equality**.
 
• This right, primarily covered under **Articles 14 to 18** of the Indian Constitution
 
• It **ensures that every individual is treated equally** before the law and prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. 
 
• **Article 15,** specifically, prohibits discrimination against any citizen and is the primary safeguard against such discrimination.
 
• **Articles 14- Equality Before Law**
 
 
• States that the state shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 16-Equality of Opportunity in Matters of Public Employmen**t
 
 
• Ensures equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 17-Abolition of Untouchability**
 
 
• Abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form
 
 
 
• **Article 18: Abolition of Titles**
 
 
• Prohibits the state from conferring any titles, except military or academic distinctions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**

 
 
• **​**This right, enshrined in **Articles 25 to 28** of the Indian Constitution, guarantees individuals the freedom to practice, profess, and propagate their religion.
 
 
 
• Right against Exploitation
 
 
• This right, detailed in **Articles 23 and 24**, prohibits human trafficking and forced labor
 
 
 
• Right to Freedom
 
 
• The **Right to Freedom** in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in **Articles 19 to 22** and guarantees various freedoms to citizens.
 
• This set of rights is crucial for ensuring individual liberty and democratic governance

questions.question: A housemaid gets her 12 - year - old daughter to help in her work as a house cleaner at a residential colony instead of sending her to school. Which fundamental duty is violated by the housemaid?

options.text: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child
To defend the country and render national service
To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide opportunities for education to his/her child**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• She **violates the fundamental duty under Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution, specifically 51A(k),
 
• It s**tates that it is the duty of every citizen to provide opportunities for education** to his or her child or,
 
 
• as the case may be, to work toward the achievement of the same.
 
 
 
• By making her 12-year-old daughter work as a house cleaner instead of sending her to school,
 
 
• the housemaid is neglecting her duty to ensure that her child receives an education.
 
 
 
• **Education is essential for the development and empowerment of children**,
 
• It is considered a fundamental responsibility of parents or guardians to facilitate this.
 
• This situation not only contravenes the fundamental duty of providing education but also raises concerns about child labor,
 
 
• which is prohibited under various laws in India, including the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A**

 
 
• **​Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution outlines the **Fundamental Duties** of citizens. 
 
• It was added by the **42nd Amendment** in 1976 
 
• It serves to remind citizens of their responsibilities toward the nation.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A enumerates **a set of **fundamental duties** that every citizen is expected to uphold.
 
• **Some of these duties include**:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.

questions.question: In which year did Galileo describe the regular, swinging motion of a pendulum by the action of gravity and acquired momentum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1602**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galileo Galilei d**iscovered the law that describes **the regular swinging motion of a pendulum in 1602**
 
• In the early 17th century, the study of motion was evolving.
 
• Before Galileo, the prevailing theories were primarily based on Aristotle's ideas, which did not accurately describe how objects moved under the influence of gravity.
 
• **A pendulum consists of** a mass (or bob) attached to a string or rod that swings back and forth under the influence of gravity.
 
• **Galileo discovered that the time taken for a pendulum to swing back and forth is constant, regardless of the as long as the angle is small. **
 
 
• **This property is known as isochronism. **
 
 
 
• He formulated ideas about acceleration due to gravity, which later influenced Isaac Newton's laws of motion.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Galileo Galilei**

 
 
• **​**Galileo was born on **February 15, 1564**, in Pisa, Italy.
 
• Galileo improved the design of the telescope and used it for astronomical observations. In **1610**,
 
• He discovered:
 
 
• **The Moons of Jupiter**:
 
 
• He observed the four largest moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto), which provided evidence against the geocentric model of the universe.
 
 
 
• **Phases of Venus**:
 
 
• He documented the phases of Venus, supporting the heliocentric model proposed by **Nicolaus Copernicus**,
 
 
• which stated that the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun.

questions.question: The central stretch of the Western Coastal Plains of India is known as the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannad plains**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The central stretch is called the Kannad Plain
 
• It is primarily located in the state of Karnataka.
 
• It extends from the **Arabian Sea** in the west to the foothills of the **Western Ghats** in the east.
 
• The Kannada Plain is characterized by a mix of flat land and low-lying hills, making it less rugged compared to the adjacent Western Ghats.
 
• The soil in the Kannada Plain is primarily **alluvial** and **lateritic**, conducive to farming

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6db57fadbe13a39345f50aaa968c0b5bd4c67f3c78c787a2625a2bcf7a4159b9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Peninsular plateau is flanked by stretch of narrow coastal strips, running along the Arabian Sea on the west and the Bay of Bengal on the east.
 
• The Western Coastal Plains
 
 
• The western coast, sandwiched between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, is a narrow plain.
 
• It consists of three sections; the northern part of the coast is called the Konkan__ (Mumbai – Goa),
 
 
• while the southern stretch is referred to as the Malabar Coast.
 
 
 
• The rivers flowing through this coastal plain do not form any delta.
 
 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains 
 
 
• The eastern coast are the plains along the Bay of Bengal are wide and level.
 
• In the northern part, it is referred to as the Northern Circar, while the southern part is known as the Coromandel Coast.
 
• There are well-developed deltas here, formed by the rivers flowing eastward in to the Bay of Bengal and include the deltas of the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri.

questions.question: In MS - Word, a document may be printed using ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl+P**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Ctrl+P is the short key used to print a document in MS Word.**
 
• Print Preview in MS Word is used to View how the document will appear when printed.
 
• Print preview refers to formatting a document for the printer.
 
• Print preview is commonly called preview or previewing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ctrl + C (Copy)**

 
 
• **​**Copies the selected text, image, or object to the clipboard.
 
• When you press **Ctrl + C**, the selected content remains in its original location, but a copy is stored in the clipboard.
 
• This allows you to paste it elsewhere without affecting the original content.
 
 
 
• **Ctrl + X** (Cut)
 
 
• Cuts the selected text, image, or object and moves it to the clipboard.
 
 
 
• **Ctrl + V** (Paste)
 
 
• Pastes the content from the clipboard to the current cursor location

questions.question: Name the Chola inscription that provided details of the way in which the sabha was organised in the local administration in the Chola empire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** the Uttaramerur inscription**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The **Uttaramerur Inscription** is the Chola inscription that provides detailed information about the organization of the **sabha** (village assembly) in the local administration during the Chola Empire
 
• It **outlines the criteria for becoming a member of the assembly**, the qualifications required for candidates, the process of electing members,
 
 
• and the responsibilities of different committees.
 
 
 
• The** inscription is found in Uttaramerur**, a village in present-day Tamil Nadu.
 
• The inscription mentions the system of **kudavolai** (lottery) for electing members to the various committees of the sabha
 
• The Uttaramerur inscription showcases the **highly decentralized administrative structure of the Chola Empire**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Darsanam Koppu Inscription**

 
 
• **It ​**refers to an inscription found during the reign of the Cholas.
 
• It is notable for its reference to land grants or donations made to temples or religious institutions.
 
• This type of inscription typically provides insights into the administrative setup during the Chola period
 
• It highlights the practice of **temple endowments** (land grants given to temples), 4
 
 
• showing the interrelationship between rulers and religious bodies in medieval India.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Thiruvalangadu Inscription**
 
 
• **​**The **Thiruvalangadu inscription** is one of the most famous Chola inscriptions, commissioned by **Rajaraja Chola I**,
 
 
• who ruled in the 11th century. It is located in the **Thiruvalangadu** temple, near Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• This inscription provides a detailed eulogy of the Chola king Rajaraja I, tracing the lineage of the Chola dynasty and celebrating his military achievements.
 
• It includes references to his conquests in South India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.
 
 
 
• **Thirunanthikarai Inscription****​**
 
 
• The Thirunanthikarai inscription shows the influence of the Ay dynasty in the region,
 
 
• providing evidence of land ownership, local governance, and religious endowments.
 
 
 
• It also highlights the cultural and economic exchanges between the different South Indian kingdoms during this period
 
• The inscription, written in **Vattezhuthu script**, records a land grant made during the reign of the **Ay kings**. 
 
 

ae:T

questions.question: Which of the following is a string instrument commonly featured in the folk music of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jantar**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jantar** is a string instrument commonly featured in the folk music of Gujarat.
 
• It is **often used in traditional performances and folk songs.**
 
• It is** made from bamboo and has a simple design with strings** stretched across a resonating box, which produces sound when the strings are plucked.
 
• The Jantar is often played by folk musicians, especially in rural areas, and is typically used to accompany singing or storytelling.
 
• It has a **deep, resonant sound **and is closely associated with tribal and nomadic communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bungal**, **Pava**, and **Turi** are wind instruments

 
 
• **Bungal**

 
 
• **It** is a traditional wind instrument, often associated with nomadic and pastoral communities of Gujarat.
 
• It is a long, curved trumpet made from copper or brass and produces a loud, piercing sound.
 
• Bungal is typically used in ceremonial music or during martial events.
 
 
 
• **Pava**
 
 
• **It** is a folk wind instrument similar to a flute.
 
• It is made from bamboo and is played by blowing air across one end while covering the finger holes to produce different notes.
 
• It is used in various folk performances and devotional music in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Turi**
 
 
• **​It** is another wind instrument, commonly used in Gujarat’s folk traditions.
 
• It is a horn-like instrument that produces a loud sound and is often played during festive or ceremonial occasions.

questions.question: In which year was the first Arjuna Award given to a woman hockey player?

The correct answer is __**1961**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first woman hockey player** to receive the Arjuna Award was **Anne Lumsden in 1961.**
 
• It is bestowed by the Government of India (Ministry of Youth Affairs and sports) to sportspersons for their outstanding performance in international
 
 
• as well as national events and also holds leadership qualities with good morals.
 
 
 
• The award was launched in 1961 with a cash prize of Rs 5 lakh, a bronze statue of Arjuna, and
 
 
• a scroll and is presented by the President of India every year to the sportspersons of different categories. 
 
 
 
• Now the Prize money is increased to 15 lakhs.
 
• The honour is named on Prince Arjuna, the protagonist of the Indian epic Mahabharata.
 
• He must have shown qualities of leadership sportsmanship and a sense of discipline.
 
• From 2001, the award is given in disciplines falling under the following categories: 
 
 
• Olympic Games/Commonwealth Games/Asian Games
 
• World Cup/World Championship disciplines and cricket;
 
• Indigenous games; and
 
• Sports for the physically challenged.
 
 
 
• The Arjuna Award was first presented in 1961 to six people.
 
• Meena Shah (Badminton) was the first woman to get the Arjuna award in 1962.
 
• The first recipient of the Arjuna Award in the field of Archery was Krishna Das awarded in 1961.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles was amended in the Constitution (Fifth Amendment Act), 1955?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 3**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1955 amended several articles of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **One significant change was the amendment to Article 3.**
 
• It d**eals with the procedure for the formation of new states **and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• The amendment clarified and reinforced the process by which the Parliament could enact changes concerning the states.
 
• It made it explicit that the President of India could initiate the process of reorganization, and the Parliament would then have the final say.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability**

 
 
• **​A**bolishes the practice of untouchability, making it illegal in India.
 
• It states that the enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability is a punishable offense under the law.
 
• The article promotes social equality by ensuring that all individuals have the right to equality before the law, irrespective of caste.
 
 
 
• **Article 34: Restriction on Rights Conferred by Part III While Martial Law is in Force**
 
 
• **​A**llows the Parliament to restrict the rights conferred by Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution during the enforcement of martial law in any area.
 
 
 
• **Article 45: Provision for Early Childhood Care and Education**
 
 
• **​D**irects the state to provide for early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of early childhood education in the holistic development of children,
 
 
• addressing their physical, mental, and social needs.

questions.question: What is known to be ‘ekaharya’, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bharatnatyam dance is a dance form of Tamil Nadu which is also known to be as ekaharya, where one dancer takes on several roles in a single performance.
 
• It is also known as Dasiattam.
 
• The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur has been a centre for Bharatanatyam since 1000 CE.
 
• In its usual form, the dance is generally divided into seven main parts – Alarippu, Jatiswaran, Shabda, Varna, Pada, Thillana and Sloka.
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai, Shobhana, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, and Chithra Vishveshwaran 
 
 
• ​are some of the famous contemporaries of the Bharatnatyam Dance form.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kathak:​

 
 
• ​This dance originated in North India.
 
• It was largely a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures.
 
 
 
• Kuchipudi:
 
 
• Kuchipudi is the name of a village in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh which has a long custom of dance-drama.
 
 
 
• Kathakali:
 
 
• Kathakali is a blend of dance, music, and acting and dramatizes stories, which are mostly adapted from Indian epics
 
• Different facial colors indicate different mental stages & characters, e.g. green – nobility, black – wicked, red patches – combining royalty & evil.

questions.question: How can you access the Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard in Microsoft Word?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clicking on the Mailings tab **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• **Step by Step Instructions **

 
 
• **Open Microsoft Word**:

 
 
• Launch Microsoft Word on your computer.
 
 
 
• **Go to the Mailings Tab:**
 
 
• At the top of the window, find and click on the "Mailings" tab in the ribbon.
 
 
 
• **Start Mail Merge**:
 
 
• In the "Mailings" tab, look for the "Start Mail Merge" group.
 
• Click on "Start Mail Merge" to see a dropdown menu.
 
 
 
• **Select Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard**:
 
 
• From the dropdown menu, select **"Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard..."**.
 
• This will open the Mail Merge task pane on the right side of your Word window.
 
 
 
• **Follow the Wizard**:
 
 
• The wizard guide you through the mail merge process with clear steps,
 
 
• including selecting the document type, choosing recipients, writing the letter, and completing the merge.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Green Revolution is/are correct?

I. India became self-reliant after the advent of the Green Revolution.

II. Due to the Green Revolution, the soil started losing nutrients due to repeated cultivation of the same crop.

III. Green revolution caused depletion of fresh ground water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i, ii and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India led to self-reliance in terms of food grain production, transforming the country from a food-deficient nation to one that could sustain itself.
 
• Repetitive cultivation of the same high-yield variety (HYV) crops led to soil nutrient depletion, as these crops absorbed specific nutrients in large quantities.
 
• The Green Revolution intensified the use of water resources for irrigation, leading to the depletion of fresh groundwater levels, especially in regions like Punjab and Haryana.
 
• The use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides increased significantly during the Green Revolution, contributing to environmental degradation and impacting soil health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period during the 1960s and 1970s when agriculture in many developing countries was transformed by the adoption of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• It aimed to increase food production to combat hunger and improve food security.
 
• Countries like India and Mexico saw significant increases in crop production, particularly in wheat and rice.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental issues, including soil degradation, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Soil Nutrient Depletion:**
 
 
• Continuous cultivation of the same crop without crop rotation can lead to the depletion of specific nutrients in the soil.
 
• This results in reduced soil fertility, necessitating the increased use of chemical fertilizers to maintain crop yields.
 
• Over time, this can lead to soil degradation and reduced agricultural sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater Depletion:**
 
 
• Intensive irrigation practices, particularly in regions with limited water resources, can lead to the over-extraction of groundwater.
 
• This can cause a decline in water tables, making it more difficult and expensive to access water for irrigation in the long term.
 
• Regions like Punjab and Haryana in India have experienced significant groundwater depletion due to the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides associated with the Green Revolution has led to environmental pollution.
 
• These chemicals can contaminate soil and water bodies, adversely affecting plant and animal life.
 
• There are also health concerns for humans exposed to these chemicals through food and water.

questions.question: What was the Child Sex Ratio in the country as per the Census of India 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**919.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the census 2001, the child sex ratio of India was 927 which declined to 919 in the census 2011. 
 
• Child sex ratio:
 
 
• The Child Sex Ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the age group 0–6 years.
 
 
 
• As per the census 2011, Arunachal Pradesh has the highest child sex ratio among the Indian states i.e. 972 while Haryana has the lowest child sex ratio i.e., 834 per thousand males. 
 
• Among the Union Territories of India; Andaman and Nicobar Islands has the highest child sex ratio i.e., 968 per thousand males. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The responsibility of conducting the decennial Census rests with the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• Census Act was enacted in 1948 to provide for the scheme of conducting population census with duties and responsibilities of census officers.
 
• Government of India decided in May 1949 to initiate steps for developing systematic collection of statistics on the size of the population, its growth, etc., and established an organisation in the Ministry of Home Affairs under Registrar General and ex-Officio Census Commissioner, India.

questions.question: Which of the following types of music is confined to the states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Carnatic**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carnatic Music__

 __
 
• Carnatic music is one of the forms of Indian classical music.
 
• It is confined to southern India, the states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamilnadu, and Kerala
 
 
• ​ while the classical music of the rest of the country is under the name of Hindustani.
 
 
 
• The main emphasis in Carnatic music is on the vocals.
 
• The music is created in the traditional octave form and the music is Kriti-based
 
 
• ​ and focuses more on the Sahithya or the lyric quality of the musical piece.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Music**

 
 
• **​**Hindustani music is a major form of classical music practised primarily in North India, dating back to the Vedic times.
 
• It is based on **ragas** (melodic frameworks) and **talas** (rhythmic cycles) with a strong emphasis on improvisation by the performer.
 
• Renowned figures like **Pandit Ravi Shankar**, **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, and **Kishori Amonkar** have popularized Hindustani music globally.
 
• Common instruments include the **sitar**, **tabla**, **sarod**, and **tanpura**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Music**
 
 
• **​**Regional music refers to folk and traditional music from different parts of India, reflecting the cultural diversity of various regions.
 
• **Bihu** (Assam), **Baul** (Bengal), **Lavani** (Maharashtra), and **Garba** (Gujarat) are popular forms of regional music.
 
• Unlike classical music, regional music often has simpler structures, with repetitive rhythms and lyrics rooted in everyday life
 
 
 
• **Classical Music**
 
 
• **​**Indian classical music is divided into two main traditions: **Hindustani (North Indian)** and **Carnatic (South Indian)**.
 
• Classical music often has spiritual undertones, used in temples and courts historically, and is meditative in nature.
 
• Well-known classical musicians include **MS Subbulakshmi** (Carnatic), **Bismillah Khan** (Shehnai), and **Zakir Hussain** (Tabla).

questions.question: Since 1994, Winter Olympics traditionally take place _____ after the Summer Olympics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 years**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Since 1994, the Winter Olympics traditionally take place **two years** after the Summer Olympics. 
 
• This change was introduced to alternate the Winter and Summer Olympics every two years, instead of holding them in the same year as was done earlier.
 
• It is a sporting event that occurs every four years.
 
• The first celebration of the Winter Olympics was held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.
 
• The original sports were alpine and cross-country skiing, figure skating, ice hockey, Nordic combined, ski jumping, and speed skating.
 
• The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were interrupted by World War II.
 
• The Olympics resumed in 1948 and were celebrated every four years.
 
• The Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years until 1992, after a 1986 decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on separate four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years.
 
• Because of the change, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.
 
• The 2022 Winter Olympics, officially known as the XXIV Olympic Winter Games and commonly known as Beijing 2022, is an international winter multi-sport event that is scheduled to take place from 4 to 20 February 2022, in Beijing and towns in the neighboring Hebei province in the People's Republic of China. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 2020 Summer Olympics commonly known as Tokyo 2020, is to be held in Tokyo, Japan.
 
• Hockey, Badminton, and Archery are the summer Olympic sports.
 
• Karate, roller sport, climbing, surfing, baseball, and softball are the recent sports added for 2020.
 
• Beijing is due to host the 2022 Winter Olympics, which will make it the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Games.
